text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canada to vote June 2: Liberals seek mandate to reshape social programs, plan for 21st century, Chretien says.
- Flood fighters flee gale forecast: Waves expected to pound dikes.
- Major refuses to admit defeat: Tory 'blood bath' warnings unheeded.
- The affluent use tutors, camp in race to give children an edge.
- Zimbabwe's glitter masks a dark side: Though new shops and new cars dot Harare's streets, signs of social and political decay are also beginning to show.
- On-line chatter roils Bre-X: News, gossip among Internet-savvy investors drives shares up and down.
- Phone firms brace for CRTC rulings: Monopolies on local service will end.
- Developer builds reputation with Budapest's biggest mall.
- Balaclava opens battle for BC Sugar.
- Mobil eyes $1-billion oilsands plan: Would join companies cashing in on healthy returns as costs are trimmed.
- After the flood: Manitoba looks at a $100-million-plus bill.
